one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban profiles Justice Samuel R. Martires, Duterte's first SC appointee, who publicly admitted at the July 27, 2017 San Beda Law Alumni testimonial dinner -- with Executive Secretary Medialdea in the audience -- that the SC was not his ultimate aspiration: his real ambition was the Ombudsman. Martires recalled tracking and admiring the author's career since his 'short-pants days' and noted he had taken his SBN oath before Panganiban on May 8, 2006. At President Duterte's birthday celebration on April 5, 2018 at Sofitel, the author privately asked why Martires hadn't applied for the soon-to-be-vacant Ombudsman post; Martires replied, 'Chief, I am still praying about it, asking the Lord for guidance' -- to which Panganiban responded, 'I will pray with you and for you.' Days later, Martires filed his application, gathered the most votes in both the JBC and the SC, and was appointed. His challenge, the column notes, is to uphold and surpass the standard of 'competence, honesty and industry' set by predecessor Conchita Carpio Morales. Martires's early SC retirement creates an additional 2018 slot for Duterte, alongside those vacated by Velasco (August 8) and De Castro (October 8), and is followed by five more in 2019 (Tijam, Del Castillo, Jardeleza, Bersamin, and Carpio). Combined with his first four 2017 appointees (Martires, Tijam, Reyes Jr., and Gesmundo), Duterte will have filled 13 of 15 SC seats by the end of his term, leaving only Leonen and Caguioa from the original bench -- this projection being the column's own cross-reference to Panganiban's broader Aug. 5 'presidential capture' concerns.
